findings.what: OUTPUT_MIN_TRACK_LEN, RESULTS probes 6/9 = CONTEXT A19/A21. OLD VERDICT: 6->4 read 0.943 (-0.002) and 6->8 read 0.944 (-0.001) on the exp06 base. 'With A19 the node-count bonus is not exploitable via track length'; post-proc probes were closed. WHAT CHANGED: tonight's risk stack (exp89q/r, 00:05Z) and exp89s carry ILP_DISAPPEARANCE_WEIGHT 2.25 because of the metric formula: '-0.73% nodes = a mechanical bonus of ~+0.0007'. R26's verifier said this bonus 'stands untouched'. MIN_TRACK_LEN is the purest public test of that premise. In exp70g cell 7 the filter drops non-division connected components smaller than the threshold, so it acts on the same short-fragment population that a higher S = A + Dis prunes inside the ILP. MEASURED: on the K dummy (exp85a CSV), non-division components of size 6-7 hold 3,317 of 122,328 nodes (2.71%). By clip: 44b6_0113 1.01%, 44b6_0b24 7.66%, 6bba_05b6 2.57%, 6bba_05db 1.93%. The official metric is J*(1 - 0.1*(N_pred - N_total)/N_total), linear with no kink, and N_pred/N_total is about 1.00 on the dense dummy clips. So min len 8 carries a gross bonus of about +0.0025, yet the lineage read -0.001. The implied edge loss is about 0.0013 per 1% of nodes removed. Applied to DIS 2.25: gross +0.00066, loss 0.00095*rho, where rho is the TP density of the DIS-removed fragments relative to length-6/7 components. The ILP chooses those fragments by low edge probability, so rho < 1 is plausible, but the dummy lab is mixed (exp89q vs exp89p identical TP/FP/FN; exp88a vs exp70g -1 TP +2 FP). Net prior about 0, range -0.0003..+0.0006. Both directions of the fragment knob read negative on public, so the lineage defaults sit at the public optimum. NEW VERDICT: MIN_TRACK_LEN stays CLOSED on K; no 7/8 arm, since it is about 3.7x the DIS dose. The closure REVIVES as evidence: the formula bonus is gross, and the only public reads of pure node-count levers did not collect it. The DIS 1.75 'closed for 29 Sep' stays closed, now on the right basis (no public support for either direction; default 2 plausibly optimal), not on the formula. Caveat: probes 6/9 ran on the old exp06 base with 3-decimal rounding, so this is an anchor, not a measurement on K.

By the same arithmetic, DIS 2.25's +0.0007 is gross, not net. The net prior is about 0 (-0.0003..+0.0006). The night does not change. Put this in the freeze and card text, prefer the non-DIS twin on an equal display, and do not flip DIS to 1.75 after the fact. (B) v3 s_merge 'whole-kernel dummy runtimes cannot judge the hidden budget' (OVERTURNED in v3): this REVIVES against rule v2 and against R26-A3's 'DIS dummies ran +15-20%'. The logs split each run into a silent setup phase of 203-788 s (machine noise) and a compute phase. Compute is stable: non-CI 1,047-1,153 s, CI 1,473-1,645 s. DIS changes compute by 0-5%, and its per-clip ILP times are equal. So exp89r's hidden latency is expected to match exp87a's, with no DIS inflation. Rule v2 should gate on compute time, so that a slow setup does not cost a ~35-min GPU re-run (for example on the exp89l dummy). (C) DET_THRESHOLD (RESULTS probe 4; knobarms v_6 'revisit only if both READMIT arms are spent and a slot is left over'): the revisit trigger has now formally fired (READMIT 0.99 dominated, 0.92/0.90 closed, morning slots default UNUSED). On K, the end-anchored part of the [0.96, 0.965) band is already readmitted at 0.94, so DET 0.96 adds only unanchored nodes, the population with <= 0 public value. DET 0.97 rests on the same node-bonus premise that (A) finds unsupported. The imissher pair is weak evidence (v3: leaky in-kernel sweeps). It is never a morning filler.
